channel.title: Full Fact - All content
channel.description: Full Fact is the UK’s independent fact checking charity

item.title: Baseless claim that Henry Kissinger gave a WHO speech about ‘mandatory forcible’ vaccinations recirculates
item.description: Social media posts are once again claiming the former US Secretary of State gave a speech about vaccinations being used as “extermination services”.

item.title: Airlines are not banning vaccinated people from flying
item.description: Similar claims have been circulating online since 2021, but there is no evidence any airline bans vaccinated people from flying.

item.title: Income tax and national debt both existed 100 years ago
Video supposedly showing Muslim woman telling people to ‘cover up’ is fake
Post from ‘Nobel Committee member’ is satire
item.description: A satirical post about Donald Trump’s efforts to be awarded the Nobel Peace Prize has been shared on Facebook as if it’s from an actual Nobel Committee member.

item.title: Toby Carvery isn’t giving away a free carvery to celebrate ‘National Yorkshire Pudding Week’
Video shows street vendors in Spain, not people selling items looted in France
item.description: A video of street vendors in Madrid selling designer bags and football shirts is being shared with false claims it shows people selling goods looted during the recent unrest in France.

item.title: AI mushroom cloud video shared with false claims it shows Ukraine
item.description: A video of a mushroom cloud explosion has been shared online with false claims about supposed Ukrainian military losses. The clip has been circulating since 2025 and was made with AI.

item.title: Donald Trump did not post on Truth Social about the Republicans already winning the 2026 midterms
item.description: Full Fact could not find any reliable evidence that President Trump’s Truth Social account shared such a post about the Republicans already winning the 2026 midterms.

item.title: Viral video doesn’t show zombie knives delivery to ‘migrant hotel’
item.description: Footage of police officers intercepting a shipment of zombie knives is being shared online with false claims that it was bound for a migrant hotel.
